Let it suffice to recall the interesting fact to your notice, and invite you to compare the respective biographies of the Brahmanical Krshna, the Persian Zoroaster, the Egyptian Hermes, the Indian Gautama, and the canonical, especially the apocryphal, Jesus.

67960-tramping-with-a-poet-in-the-rockie.title: In The Rockies
67960-tramping-with-a-poet-in-the-rockie.creator: Stephen Graham
67960-tramping-with-a-poet-in-the-rockie.description: A book by Stephen Graham. Vachel Lindsay was an art student before he was a poet, and wrote his first verses as scrolls to be illuminated below emblematic figures, we naturally discussed emblems and emblematic art and hieroglyphics as we tramped together. The emblems in this book are an attempt to express that side of our mutual experience. They have been done by my friend, Vernon Hill, who drew once that very precious work, “The Arcadian Calendar.”

arxiv-2302-01112.creator: W. H. T. Vlemmings ,, D. Tafoya
arxiv-2302-01112.description: Abstract Context. arxiv-2311-07806.title: Assessing Test-time Variability for Interactive 3D Medical Image Segmentation with Diverse Point Prompts
arxiv-2311-07806.creator: Hao Li, Han Liu, Dewei Hu, Jiacheng Wang, Ipek Oguz
arxiv-2311-07806.description: Abstract Interactive segmentation model leverages prompts from users to produce robust segmentation. This advancement is facilitated by prompt engineering, where interactive prompts serve as strong priors during test-time. However, this is an inherently subjective and hard-to-reproduce process. The variability in user expertise and inherently ambiguous boundaries in medical images can lead to inconsistent prompt selections, potentially affecting segmentation accuracy.

arxiv-2401-00641.title: Hierarchical Bayesian Modeling for Time-Dependent Inverse Uncertainty Quantification
arxiv-2401-00641.creator: Chen Wang
arxiv-2401-00641.description: Abstract This paper introduces a novel hierarchical Bayesian model specifically designed to address challenges in Inverse Uncertainty Quantification (IUQ) for time-dependent problems in nuclear Thermal Hydraulics (TH) systems. The unique characteristics of time-dependent data, such as high dimensionality and correlation in model outputs requires special attention in the IUQ process.

pmc-10561996.title: Cardiovascular Hospitalizations and Hospitalization Costs in Japan During the COVID-19 Pandemic
pmc-10561996.creator: Tadafumi Sugimoto, Atsushi Mizuno, Daisuke Yoneoka, Shingo Matsumoto, Chisa Matsumoto, Yuya Matsue, Mari Ishida, Michikazu Nakai, Yoshitaka Iwanaga, Yoshihiro Miyamoto, Koichi Node
pmc-10561996.description: BackgroundDuring the COVID-19 pandemic, cardiovascular hospitalizations decreased and in-hospital mortality for ST-elevation myocardial infarction and heart failure increased. However, limited research has been conducted on hospitalization and mortality rates for cardiovascular disease (CVD) other than ischemic heart disease and heart failure.

pmc-10753461.title: Traits and skills of effective leaders in antimicrobial stewardship
pmc-10753461.creator: Tanaya Bhowmick, Ahmed Abdul Azim, Navaneeth Narayanan, Keith Kaye
pmc-10753461.description: differences between leadership and management, and skills and traits important for both roles to be effective. While leadership is the focus of this manuscript, leaders in stewardship often directly oversee and manage at least some components of the stewardship program, and therefore, effective leaders in stewardship should be familiar with skills and traits necessary for effective management.

pmc-11313262.title: Self-Management among Stroke Survivors in the United States, 2016 to 2021
pmc-11313262.creator: Ajith Kumar Vemuri, Seyyed Sina Hejazian, Alireza Vafaei Sadr, Shouhao Zhou, Keith Decker, Jonathan Hakun, Vida Abedi, Ramin Zand, Jussi Sipilä
pmc-11313262.description: Background: Self-management among stroke survivors is effective in mitigating the risk of a recurrent stroke. This study aims to determine the prevalence of self-management and its associated factors among stroke survivors in the United States. Methods: We analyzed the Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System (BRFSS) data from 2016 to 2021, a nationally representative health survey.

pmc-11373534.title: Parahydrogen-enhanced pH measurements using [1-13C]bicarbonate derived from non-enzymatic decarboxylation of [1-13C]pyruvate-d3†
pmc-11373534.creator: Maria Daniela Santi, Theresa Luca Katrin Hune, Gonzalo Gabriel Rodriguez, Lisa M. Fries, Ruhuai Mei, Sonja Sternkopf, Josef Elsaßer, Stefan Glöggler
pmc-11373534.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Alterations in pH are a hallmark in several pathologies including cancer, ischemia, and inflammation. Non-invasive magnetic resonance methods to measure pH offer a new approach for early diagnosis of diseases characterized by acid–base imbalances. The hyperpolarization with parahydrogen-induced polarization (PHIP) enhances inherently low signals in magnetic resonance experiments by several orders of magnitude and offers a suitable platform to obtain biocompatible markers in less than one minute.

pmc-11477557.title: Epimesatines P–S: Four Undescribed Flavonoids from Epimedium sagittatum Maxim. and Their Cytotoxicity Activities
pmc-11477557.creator: Shuang-Shuang Xie, Xiang Yu, Jing-Ke Zhang, Zhi-You Hao, Xiao-Ke Zheng, Wei-Sheng Feng, George Grant
pmc-11477557.description: In this study, four previously undescribed flavonoids, named epimesatines P (1), Q (2), R (3), and S (4), were isolated from the aerial parts of Epimedium sagittatum Maxim. Their structures and absolute configurations were confirmed via spectroscopic analyses, quantum chemical electronic circular dichroism (ECD) calculations, Mo2(OAc)4–induced ECD, and Rh2(OCOCF3)4–induced ECD experiments.

pmc-12561468.title: Acupuncture–Moxibustion Combined with Locomotor Training Enhances Postoperative Recovery in Canine Cervical Intervertebral Disc Herniation: A Pilot Study
pmc-12561468.creator: Tianyu Wang, Dongchun Jin, Wen Cui, Jincheng Bai, Han Zhang, Jiayi Wang, Inseong Jeong, Xinmei Jin, Namsoo Kim, Zhenglin Piao, Mandy Paterson
pmc-12561468.description: Simple SummaryCanine Cervical Intervertebral Disc Herniation is a common neurological disorder in clinical practice. While ventral slot decompression effectively relieves spinal cord compression, postoperative functional recovery remains highly dependent on rehabilitation therapy. Existing studies indicate that multimodal exercise training or combined adjunctive therapies demonstrate certain efficacy, yet their effectiveness remains limited in cases with severe neurological deficits.

pmc-13094189.title: Enteral olive oil supplementation as a rescue strategy for caloric insufficiency in critically ill neonates: a retrospective cohort study
pmc-13094189.creator: Ferid Aliyev, Ece Karatas, Damla Yıldırım, Gozdem Kayki, Sule Yigit
pmc-13094189.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ObjectiveTo evaluate the feasibility and short-term growth outcomes associated with enteral olive oil supplementation in critically ill neonates who were unable to meet daily caloric requirements due to feeding intolerance or fluid restrictions.MethodsThis retrospective cohort study included 38 neonates admitted to a Level IV neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) between January 2018 and January 2025 who received enteral olive oil supplementation because of insufficient caloric intake despite standard nutritional interventions.

pmc-13156566.title: Superselective intra-arterial infusion of cisplatin and concomitant radiation therapy (RADPLAT) using gadolinium-based contrast agent in a patient with severe iodine allergy: A case report
pmc-13156566.creator: Yume Sanji, Mizuki Ozawa, Seiya Mochizuki, Yuko Kubo, Madoka Sakuramachi, Hideaki Takahashi, Akane Yoshiba, Go Omura, Miyuki Sone
pmc-13156566.description: Maxillary sinus squamous cell carcinoma (MS-SCC) is a rare malignancy that is often diagnosed at an advanced stage. We report a case of locally advanced MS-SCC that was successfully treated with super-selective intra-arterial cisplatin infusion concurrent with radiotherapy (RADPLAT) using gadolinium-based contrast agents due to a severe allergy to iodinated contrast media.

pmc-13282610.title: Lifestyle triggers of migraine: Sleep restriction and caffeine lower the threshold for migraine‐like responses in rats in a sex‐specific manner
pmc-13282610.creator: Gabriel Camargo de Oliveira, Darciane Favero Baggio, Vanessa Bordenowsky Pereira Lejeune, Laura Storithont Quinelato, Fernanda Mariano Ribeiro da Luz, Aleksander Roberto Zampronio, Luana Fischer, Juliana Geremias Chichorro
pmc-13282610.description: ObjectiveThis study explores whether sleep restriction (SR) and caffeine intake affect migraine susceptibility by testing if each condition, alone or in combination, precipitates migraine‐like responses to subthreshold doses of calcitonin gene‐related peptide (CGRP) or pituitary adenylate cyclase‐activating polypeptide (PACAP) in male and female rats.

pmc-13383067.creator: Tengyu Liu, Jinshu Huang, Qizhi Luo, Song Yang, Anders Riisager, Hu Li
pmc-13383067.description: Heterogeneous photocatalysis has emerged as a green solution for converting renewable biomass into biofuels and chemicals, though it typically suffers from unsatisfactory carbon utilization efficiency. Here, we present a “two‐in‐one” photoreduction strategy enabled by electron‐rich Cd sites, both remote from and adjacent to sulfur vacancies (Vs).

pmc-13432549.title: Olfactory Bulb Volume Reflects Olfactory Dysfunction and Network Organization: Insights From the Population‐Based Rhineland Study
pmc-13432549.creator: Weiyi Zeng, Konstantinos Melas, Santiago Estrada, N. Ahmad Aziz, Monique M. B. Breteler
pmc-13432549.description: BackgroundOlfactory dysfunction is common in aging and an early symptom of neurodegenerative diseases, but how structural (olfactory bulb [OB] volume) and functional (olfactory network [OFN] functional connectivity [FC]) brain features interact to shape odor identification ability remains unclear. Therefore, we assessed the interrelations among OB volume, OFN FC, and odor identification ability in a large population‐based cohort.
